module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Well totally dominated graphs

A *total dominating set* of `G` is a set `S` of vertices such that every vertex of `G`
(including vertices in `S`) has a neighbor in `S`. A total dominating set `S` is
*minimal* if no proper subset of `S` is also a total dominating set.

A graph `G` is *well totally dominated* if every minimal total dominating set has the
same cardinality; equivalently, the total domination number equals the maximum
cardinality of a minimal total dominating set.

The *pendant vertices* (also called *leaves*) of `G` are the vertices of degree 1.
-/

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- A set `S` is a total dominating set of `G` if every vertex has a neighbor in `S`. -/
def IsTotalDominatingSet (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : α, ∃ w ∈ S, G.Adj v w

/-- A total dominating set `S` is minimal if no proper subset of `S` is also a
total dominating set. -/
def IsMinimalTotalDominatingSet (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S : Finset α) : Prop :=
  IsTotalDominatingSet G S ∧
  ∀ T : Finset α, T ⊂ S → ¬IsTotalDominatingSet G T

/-- A graph `G` is well totally dominated if every minimal total dominating set
has the same cardinality. -/
def IsWellTotallyDominated (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  ∀ S T : Finset α,
    IsMinimalTotalDominatingSet G S →
    IsMinimalTotalDominatingSet G T →
    S.card = T.card

/-- The set of pendant vertices (leaves) of `G`: vertices of degree 1. -/
noncomputable def pendantVertices (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Finset α :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun v => G.degree v = 1)

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: The `[Fintype α]` section variable on line 39 is not retained in this declaration's elaborated signature. Consequently, `IsWellTotallyDominated` accepts infinite graphs but compares only minimal total dominating sets represented by `Finset α`, not every minimal total dominating set as advertised. This distinction is substantive: take countably many disjoint edges and add an apex adjacent to every endpoint. Every finite total dominating set must contain the apex, and every minimal finite total dominating set consists of the apex and one endpoint, so Lean's predicate holds. However, the set of all endpoints is an infinite inclusion-minimal total dominating set; together with an apex–endpoint pair, it witnesses failure of the advertised equal-cardinality property. This connected, isolate-free counterexample and both minimality claims are proved without `sorry` in `/workspace/review/infinite.lean`. All five existing problem use sites assume finite vertex types, so they are unaffected by this exposed-domain defect.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII's glossary, entry 99, defines a well-total-dominated graph as one in which 'every minimal total dominating set is a minimum total dominating set'; the relevant problem section considers simple connected graphs of finite order greater than one. See https://web.archive.org/web/20260723211215id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js and the section preceding Conjecture 314 in the archived all.html. Bahadır, Ekim and Gözüpek, 'Well-totally-dominated graphs', §1, p.210 (https://doi.org/10.26493/1855-3974.2465.571), define total dominating sets as subsets of V(G) and WTD by every minimal such set having the same size. Neither definition describes the finite-set-only property on unrestricted infinite graphs. The declaration's own docstring likewise says 'every minimal total dominating set'.
findings.suggested_fix: Put a finiteness assumption explicitly in this declaration's binders, for example `def IsWellTotallyDominated (G : SimpleGraph α) [Fintype α] [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop := ...`. An unused section variable does not impose that restriction. Alternatively, if infinite graphs are intentionally supported, quantify over `Set α`, use set-based total domination and inclusion-minimality, and compare actual cardinalities. The first two definitions remain correct for their finite-set arguments even in infinite ambient graphs.

reformulations.difference: On finite graphs, Lean compares the cardinalities of all minimal total dominating sets, whereas WOWII says every minimal total dominating set is minimum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite total dominating set T contains an inclusion-minimal total dominating subset U. If all minimal sets have equal cardinality, a minimal S satisfies |S| = |U| ≤ |T|, hence is minimum. Conversely, two minimum sets have equal cardinality. Finset and Set formulations agree on finite vertex types. The exact all-subsets equivalence is proved as `Review.well_iff_every_minimal_set_is_minimum` in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`. This equivalence is restricted to finite ambient graphs; it does not resolve the infinite-domain defect reported above.

reformulations.difference: The source assumes n > 1, while Lean assumes connectivity without explicitly requiring a nontrivial vertex type.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectivity excludes the empty graph. The only additional case is a one-vertex graph, whose independence number is 1 and pendant count is 0, so the equality hypothesis cannot hold. Those boundary values were checked in Lean; a separate whole-conjecture equivalence was not written.

reformulations.difference: The source assumes n > 1, while Lean permits the connected one-vertex graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For the one-vertex graph, the complement's average degree and the pendant count are both zero. There is no total dominating set, so the universal well-total-domination conclusion holds, just as the source glossary's 'every minimal is minimum' property does. Thus the extra case adds a true instance and does not change the universal assertion. The singleton computations and the general equivalence `IsWellTotallyDominated G ↔ (Nontrivial α → IsWellTotallyDominated G)` were proved in the scratch files; no separate whole-conjecture equivalence was written.

reformulations.difference: The universally quantified assertion on the right of `answer(False) ↔` omits the source's n > 1 restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectivity excludes empty vertex types. On a one-vertex graph, both the domination number and independent domination number are 1, so the premise 3γ(G) = γᵢ(G) is false. Including this case therefore leaves the universally quantified assertion, and its negative answer, unchanged. The singleton invariant values were checked in Lean; no separate whole-conjecture equivalence was written.

review.notes: Checked all four definitions and all five problem use sites. The other three definitions agree with their standard meanings; in particular, minimality of a finite total dominating set agrees with minimality of its coerced Set even in infinite ambient graphs. Small-instance tests cover empty and isolated graphs, K₂, K₃, P₃–P₅, C₅ and C₆. The P₅ test distinguishes inclusion-minimal sets of sizes 3 and 4. Independent enumeration also verifies GraphConjecture327's stated counterexample. Relevant completed experiments are scratch.lean, infinite.lean, compute.lean, use_sites.lean and signatures.lean under /workspace/review/. The principal equivalence and counterexample proofs have no sorryAx dependencies. No separate isolated-vertex finding is warranted: both the Lean predicate and WOWII's literal universal definition are vacuous when no total dominating set exists. The archived WOWII list retains old open labels, which do not justify undoing newer solution records. No checkout files were edited, and the target matches the specified commit.

submission.summary: Added an explicit Fintype parameter to IsWellTotallyDominated and documented its finite-graph scope. Moved the section-level Fintype assumption to pendantVertices to avoid overlapping instances while preserving all other declarations' signatures and bodies. Verified that finite-graph behavior is unchanged, infinite vertex types are rejected, and the required compile command reports no errors or warnings.
